name: forest south edge: trunk band under the canopy
label: jp_city/jp-forest-bl-band-M-0
reasons: 화풍: 칸 정보량이 기준보다 훨씬 낮음 (4/4)

surfaces.part: trunk band (brown trunk in dark foliage)

answer.evidence: The 16x16 tile is a full-width foliage/trunk band: leaf canopy in rows 0-4, a brown trunk (x~4-11) in rows 5-10 seen face-on, and grass tufts in rows 11-15. The width profile is 16 for rows 0-10, so there is no ellipse, no band ending in a front-edge line, no eave shadow, and no visible contents. The trunk is a vertical face only, with no horizontal top surface. It reads as a flat front elevation, which suits a tile meant to be a tiling edge band.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a single 16x16 tile showing a dark trunk under a green canopy fringe. It has only 12 distinct colours, against a median of 108-109 per tile in the references (427 and 567 colours in total). Its greens and browns step through only about 3 lightness levels per material, while the references use 5-6 with clumped leaf highlights. Flat-fill coverage is 0% and the dark edge pixels are tinted rather than neutral, so the outline reads as dark material tone, not black. This is a small tile piece, but even allowing for that, the tile carries a tenth of the reference density. The leaf clumps are not varied and the trunk has little bark grain, so it looks flatter and simpler beside the references. A careful artist would not accept it next to them.
